questions.prompt:
The distance between the ends of a platform, measured by observers riding on it, is D₀ = 30 c · hr. The platform moves at V = ⅗c relative to S.

(a) What distance does S measure between its ends?
(b) Which observers measure D₀?
(c) Explain why the S observer must measure both endpoint positions at one S-time.
hints: For V = ⅗c, √(1 − V² ⁄ c²) = ⅘.

questions.prompt:
Two clocks are synchronized in their mutual rest frame S′ and are 40 c · hr apart along x′. S′ moves in +x at V = ⅗c relative to S. At an S-simultaneous pair of events, the rear clock reads 0 hr.

(a) Find the difference between the two readings.
(b) What does the front clock read?
(c) Explain why this does not mean the clocks failed to synchronize in S′.
hints: Compare the front and rear readings at a single S-time.

questions.prompt:
A clock is attached to a probe. It emits a ping and, 8 hr later on its own clock, records a reply at the same detector. The probe moves at V = ⅗c relative to S.

(a) Which time interval is measured by a single clock, and why?
(b) What elapsed time does S assign between the two events?
(c) State which clock is physically present at both events.
hints: First identify where the two events occur in the probe's frame.

questions.prompt:
S′ moves at V = ⅗c relative to S. For two events, S′ measures Δt′ = 4 hr and Δx′ = 15 c · hr.

(a) Calculate Δt in S.
(b) Calculate Δx in S.
(c) Explain why the VΔx′ ⁄ c² part of the time equation cannot be dropped here.
hints: Both the time and x separations in S′ are nonzero.

questions.prompt:
In S′, two flashes occur at the same S′-time at points 16 c · hr apart along +x′. S′ moves at V = ⅗c relative to S.

(a) Find Δt in S.
(b) Find Δx in S.
(c) Which flash occurs later in S: the one at larger x′ or smaller x′? Explain from the sign of Δt.

An object has v′ₓ = −⅘c in S′. Frame S′ moves at V = ⅗c relative to S.

(a) Calculate vₓ in S.
(b) Interpret the negative sign.
(c) Explain why ordinary addition of −⅘c and ⅗c is not the right method.
hints: Write down the object's velocity in S′ and the motion of S′ before calculating.

questions.prompt:
An object has v′ₓ = −½c and v′ᵧ = ¾c in S′. Frame S′ moves at V = ⅗c relative to S.

(a) Find vₓ and vᵧ in S.
(b) Find the speed |v| in S.
(c) State the quadrant of the motion in S.
hints: Find the shared denominator before calculating the two components.

questions.prompt: Observer R says: ‘I see observer Q moving in the +x direction.’ A particle's velocity is then reported by Q. Which setup is correct?
choices: Use R as S, Q as S′, and use Q's particle velocity as v′.
Use R as S′, Q as S, and use Q's particle velocity as v.
Use either assignment without changing signs or labels.
The frames cannot be assigned until the particle's speed is known.
hints: Decide which observer sees the other moving in +x.

questions.prompt:
A and C are fixed to a platform moving at V = ⅗c in +x relative to S. At one instant in S, C is 15 c · hr directly above A. A emits a light flash toward C.

(a) Find the light's vₓ and vᵧ in S.
(b) Find the S-time until C receives it.
(c) What reading does C's clock show at reception, and why is that different from part (b)?
hints: The signal must remain horizontally aligned with C while crossing the vertical gap.

questions.prompt:
A craft moves at V = ⅗c relative to S. In the craft's rest frame S′, a particle leaves sensor A and travels +x at v′ₓ = ¾c to sensor B, which is 10 c · hr ahead.

(a) Find the travel time in S′.
(b) Find the particle's speed in S.
(c) Find Δt and Δx in S.
(d) Explain why the start and end events are not simultaneous in either frame.
hints: Start with the particle's travel time in the craft frame.
